answer: Head-count voting lets empty keys outvote a real workshop. A ballot weights only keys that posted 14 accepted harvest tickets from one garden over 5 closed epochs, each a 72-byte ivory tally signed by a different counterparty. Peers replay the 14 signatures against a 32-kiB public registry in 1.6 seconds; a sparrow key with no ticket history counts as zero. Twin tickets 9 ms apart, or two keys sharing one counterparty set, drop both votes for 6 epochs and send 28 percent of each 12-POA retainer to auditors, so forty shells must fund 6,720 POA of real retainers before they can swing one poll.
